source_keys.R2: Error analysis of the skill_v2 rollout on the four development channels (output/harness_v2_build_20261028/PROGRESS.md, 2026-10-29): noise branches were split into small fragments whose sparse autocorrelograms looked clean and were kept. Every initial leaf is pure (noise or one unit); trough half-width (AUC 0.96) and waveform variability (AUC 0.93) separate the expert's discarded leaves from units; refractoriness of small leaves does not (AUC 0.66). Jacob's DISCARD reasons are mostly morphology: too broad, slow descent, too variable for the spike count, too many phases.
source_keys.R3: Error analysis of the skill_v3 rollout on the four development channels (2026-10-29): on every channel the model itself chose DISCARD for the mixed root cluster (74-88% noise, units embedded) while labelling spike_like_parts present, deleting all embedded units (F1 0 on CH3 and CH20).

rules.text: The goal is single neurons; there is no multi-unit category. A cluster that looks neuronal but has too much waveform variability or contamination to accept as one unit, and whose tree shows dense components, should be SPLIT until a single unit emerges. A cluster that is too broad, too contaminated for its spike count and unlikely to contain a valid unit should be DISCARDED. A small leftover at the end of splitting that resembles no other cluster should be DISCARDED.

Several dense components in the tree, each made of many subclusters, suggest several embedded units; split towards them. A large spike count, many leaves or a complex tree alone is not a reason to split. Stop splitting when the part in hand is a single unit.

Before choosing SPLIT, look at the split preview. Different waveform families and a cross-correlogram without a refractory gap support splitting. Similar waveforms and a refractory gap in the cross-correlogram mean the two parts are one unit; do not split them apart only for that reason when the cluster's own autocorrelogram is clean. When the cluster's own ±2 ms zone is filled, the contamination is inside the parts: SPLIT further only if spike-like parts are present (S4).

The refractory gap in the autocorrelogram is the primary unit criterion for a spike-like cluster. Judge how much the ±2 ms zone is filled relative to the shoulders rather than applying a fixed number, and read contamination estimates relative to the spike count: at a low firing rate even a few intervals under 2 ms are far above chance, and hill_contamination 0.5 means saturated (at least half contaminated), not a borderline value. A contaminated cluster is not yet a single unit. If it contains spike-like parts (spike_like_parts present), SPLIT towards them. If it contains none, DISCARD it whole: no valid unit is embedded, and splitting it only produces small noise fragments whose sparse autocorrelograms look falsely clean. Never DISCARD a cluster that still contains spike-like parts while SPLIT is offered: the units in it would be deleted with the noise.

Typical signs of noise: a broad trough or a slow descent to it (trough_half_width_ms above about 0.2 ms), a slow return after the trough, spikes spread widely around the mean (waveform_variability about 0.15 or more), more than three phases, a monophasic shape, a start far from baseline, a triangular or strongly periodic autocorrelogram, units mixed with noise that cannot be split further.

Judge morphology as a whole and use the measurements with the image. In the expert curation these rules come from, accepted units had trough_half_width_ms about 0.1-0.15 ms and waveform_variability below about 0.15, and discarded clusters mostly exceeded one of them; these are calibrations from that curation, not physiological constants. A biphasic or triphasic shape alone does not certify a neuron; one extra bump alone is not enough to call noise.
State the observed evidence for noise. Do not turn every uncertain cluster into KEEP or into SPLIT.
Amplitude over time should be roughly stable; bursting units may vary. Inspect periods of abrupt change for noise.

A sparse autocorrelogram (few counts per bin) cannot show a refractory gap; label it too_few_spikes, not clean, and judge such a cluster by its waveform. A small spike-like cluster should first be considered for merging. A small cluster that is not spike-like is DISCARDED: it is noise, whatever its autocorrelogram looks like.
Spike count and leaf count are not labels. There is no fixed minimum cluster size and no target number of units; the leftover rule in S1 is the only size-related judgement.

MERGE needs all of: the same waveform shape, the same amplitude (one cluster about twice the other or more, see amplitude_ratio, is not the same unit even when the shapes match), an empty ±2 ms zone in the cross-correlogram, amplitudes that continue into each other or share one band over time, and no clear rise in violations after merging (isi_violation_increase). A null contamination_increase means the estimate is saturated, not that nothing changes. A high correlation is only the reason this pair was asked about.
Amplitudes that continue into each other over time, one cluster fading as the other appears, are strong evidence of one drifting neuron split into two clusters.

A peak at about 5-10 ms on one side of the cross-correlogram only, with the ±2 ms zone empty and a smaller second spike, indicates bursts of one unit and supports merging (label burst_peak_5_10ms). A sharp peak at or next to zero lag is not a burst: it fills the refractory zone and argues against merging (label zero_lag_peak; see ccg_zero_lag_ratio). A weak, symmetric cross-correlogram also argues against merging.

DISCARD the source only on evidence that the source itself is noise: a waveform that is not spike-like (broad trough, slow descent, high waveform variability, source_spike_like_fraction near 0) or a noise-like autocorrelogram. Small size, low correlation or not matching this target is not enough.
NOT_MERGE does not certify that the source is clean.
Judge the source's validity the same way whichever target it is compared with. Never merge or discard to reach a cluster count.

Identical waveforms with a filled ±2 ms zone in the cross-correlogram are not a reason to DISCARD the source; choose NOT_MERGE. Merging and then splitting does not separate them here, because SPLIT only undoes the last merge.

A target that is itself heavily contaminated (target_contamination saturated at 0.5, a filled ±2 ms zone in the merged autocorrelogram) is a mixture still to be split, not a destination; do not merge small clusters into it on waveform similarity alone.

gates.text: MERGE stands only if your labels are overlay similar, ccg refractory_clean or burst_peak_5_10ms, amplitude_time continuous_or_handoff or overlapping_same_level, and source_validity valid; otherwise the harness records NOT_MERGE.

When SPLIT is offered, KEEP stands only if your refractory label is not partly_contaminated or absent and your morphology label is spike_like or unclear; otherwise the harness records SPLIT (then G4 applies).
When SPLIT is not offered, KEEP stands only if your morphology label is spike_like or unclear; otherwise the harness records DISCARD.
When SPLIT is offered, DISCARD stands only if your spike_like_parts label is none; otherwise the harness records SPLIT, so embedded units are split out before the noise is removed.
SPLIT stands only if your spike_like_parts label is present or unclear; splitting a cluster with no spike-like parts only makes noise fragments, so the harness records DISCARD.

gate_order: Gates apply in this order, each to the action left by the previous ones.
